scope: Proposition 3.4 (Approximation by power factors) of the manuscript “The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global function fields” (preprints/The-Margulis-Platonov-conjecture-over-global-function-fields-October-5-2026/margulis-platonov-global-function-fields.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 018 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7e90f88648f7bafc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let k be a global function field, let S = SU(D, ∗) be k-anisotropic of degree n ≥ 3, and put R = S(k)e for e ≥ 1. Let X = x∗S with x∗ ∈ U(k), fix γ ∈ S(k), and set C = x∗γR ⊂ X(k). Let Y ⊂ X be closed of geometric codimension at least two. Fix the torus, Galois splitting field, cocharacter and map η of (3.1). Let B be a finite set containing A, the exceptions for the fixed models, and a place v0 at which S is isotropic. At B, prescribe nonempty local open subsets of X(kv) whose product meets the closure of C given by Proposition 2.4. Let (Uv)v / ∈B be a family of subsets Uv ⊂ X(kv) satisfying the following conditions: (i) For every v / ∈ B, each integral point whose reduction avoids Y belongs to Uv. (ii) For every v / ∈ B, the set Uv contains a nonempty local open subset. (iii) There are two disjoint consecutive basic lists and, for each number of appended factors, a fixed finite family of algebraic pole tests, independent of v. After the initial point and conjugators have been fixed, these tests imply membership in Uv at every single-pole reduction outside one finite set of model exceptions. The tests admit choices in the following order. The conjugator tuple of the two basic lists may be chosen in a nonempty Zariski open subset. For each such tuple, the initial point x may be chosen in a nonempty Zariski open subset of X. For every such x and every prescribed finite number of appended factors, their conjugators may be chosen in a nonempty Zariski open subset of the corresponding power of S. For each tuple so chosen, the tests define a nonempty open subset of every absolute boundary hyperplane away from the other hyperplanes. Setting appended parameters to 1 preserves all previously available pole tests. Then there is x′ ∈ C satisfying the prescribed open conditions at B and belonging to Uv for every v / ∈ B. Finitely many additional nonempty Zariski open conditions may be imposed at the three stages in (iii), as long as they remain compatible with the stipulated choices.
